extracted.intended_audience: readers of Popular Science Monthly (educated general public, scientists, and professionals interested in natural science and scientific books)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative notices and short scientific reports reviewing books, periodicals, and short scientific/miscellaneous notes for a popular-science magazine audience; focuses on accuracy, usefulness, style, and production. Includes brief summaries of experiments, historical claims, and ethnographic/technical observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical usefulness to target audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Prof. Riley's object in publishing ... is a practical one — namely, to acquaint the farmer with the means of counteracting this plague.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A work aimed at practitioners (e.g., farmers) should emphasize actionable information and countermeasures relevant to their needs rather than abstruse theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of technicalities; popular intelligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Hence he, as far as possible, avoids technicalities, and writes in a style easily intelligible to the popular mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing for a lay or popular audience, authors should minimize technical jargon and adopt clear, accessible prose so the material is comprehensible to non-specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of authentic sources and concise presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The matter is gathered in every instance from the most authentic sources, and is presented to the reader in the smallest possible compass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compilations and reference volumes should rely on authoritative sources and present material compactly and clearly for reference value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent value and broad utility
rubrics_metrics.description: The work is one of permanent value. It is full of useful information for men in every walk of life, as the farmer, the mechanic, the merchant, the publicist, the schoolmaster, the man of letters, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate works for enduring usefulness across multiple professions and for their utility as long-term reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical authenticity and verification of contested claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The authenticity of these laws has been called in question ... The object of the editor in republishing the work is to make the public acquainted with the side of the question opposed to that of Mr. Trumbull, and to confirm, as far as possible, by contemporary testimony, the truthfulness of Dr. Peters's summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting contested historical material, editors/authors should acknowledge disputes and seek contemporary documentation or testimony to verify claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and usefulness of illustrations and maps
rubrics_metrics.description: The Locust-Plague in the United States. ... With numerous Illustrations and Colored Maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For practical works (e.g., on pests or geography), high-quality illustrations and maps materially increase usefulness and should be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of commercial puffery and unsupported dogma
rubrics_metrics.description: These so-called essays ... are really written to puff a lot of preparations sold by the author ... He dogmatically asserts his ability to furnish specific material ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific or medical writings should avoid being promotional; claims must be evidence-based and not veiled advertisements for products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific accuracy and systematic cataloguing in taxonomic works
rubrics_metrics.description: The fishes have been catalogued and described with scientific accuracy, the localities, relative abundance, and common names, are given, while the synonyms of their nomenclature receive due attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxonomic or faunal works should provide accurate descriptions, localities, abundance information, common names, and synonymy to be scientifically useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope trade-offs: depth versus breadth for specialist authors
rubrics_metrics.description: No attempt is made to give any account of the seasons, habits, or manner of breeding, which would be of most interest to the lay reader; but this would, perhaps, be too much to expect of the scientific worker attempting to cover so much ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should note realistic expectations: comprehensive coverage (including natural history details) may be impractical when the author addresses a wide taxonomic or geographic scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of physical production (printing, typography, paper, layout)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is finely printed in large, clear type, on excellent paper, with ample margins, presenting a most creditable appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodicals and books should be judged partly on production values — clear typography, good paper, and thoughtful layout contribute to readability and professional appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of content to the venue's mission and readership
rubrics_metrics.description: The projectors of this periodical are of the opinion that the metallurgical industries have become sufficiently important to have a current literature of their own, and intend that this Review shall be a vehicle for discussions on purely scientific topics, which are too abstruse for newspapers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should match the intended medium: highly technical, abstruse material belongs in specialized reviews rather than general newspapers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear description of experimental methods and controlled conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine the length of time that bees can continue to fly about, Donhoff took some of those insects ... placed them under a glass bell at a temperature of 66° Fahr. ... After forty-five minutes they all sat quietly together ... The author then fed the others with a sugar solution ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports of experiments should state apparatus, exact conditions (temperature, durations), procedures, controls, and observable measures so readers can assess validity and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of observable, measurable outcomes and physiological interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Donhoff's conclusion ... that the bee 'loses the power of flying because it does not possess the necessary strength to be converted into muscular action, and that this strength returns to its system because in sugar it finds the necessary vital support.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental reports should link measured outcomes to plausible physiological explanations while acknowledging limits of inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based handling of priority and historical invention claims
rubrics_metrics.description: As is the case with all great inventions, the telephone is now said to be nothing new; ... In the Count du Moncefs 'Expose des Applications de l'Electricite' ... occurs the following passage (translated in Nature): '... the electric transmission of sounds is not impossible. ... An electric battery, two vibrating plates, and a metallic wire, will suffice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When discussing invention priority, provide documentary citations, translations, and weigh the relative strength of prior claims rather than asserting novelty without context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced interpretation and caution in speculative theorizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Devolution or succession appears to be the law of Nature; evolution (in its modern interpretation) may be regarded as the product of human imagination. ... The notorious imperfection of the geological record ought to warn us against such hasty theorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and reviewers should recognize uncertainty, avoid overreaching conclusions from incomplete evidence, and advise caution where data are fragmentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed descriptive reporting in ethnography and natural history
rubrics_metrics.description: The natives of the Andaman Islands are described ... In height they vary from four feet nine inches to five feet one inch; they are extremely black ... They cover their bodies with red earth, and, as ornaments, wear strings of their ancestors' bones ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethnographic and natural-history notes should provide concrete measurements, material culture, and behavioral observations; reviewers should also be alert to and annotate potential bias or sensational language.
